chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the crops from which zakat is due, so he said: 'Wheat, barley, millet, drought-resistant grain, rice, salt, lentils, and sesame; all of these are subject to zakat, and their like.'
ai.seo_question: Which agricultural crops are subject to zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies the scope of zakat on agricultural produce by listing specific staples like wheat, barley, and rice, while establishing the legal principle of 'qiyas' (analogy) to include similar grains. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining which crops are subject to the one-tenth or one-half tithe based on irrigation methods, reflecting the practical economic needs of the community. The inclusion of legumes and rice highlights the comprehensive nature of zakat obligations on all major food sources cultivated from the earth.
